lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.11 - A Listen, point and say

details: Listen, point and say checks understanding of new key phrases. Listen and point checks sound-image recognition as they point to each picture. Say practises pronunciation as they repeat the key phrases
Look for careful listening, correct pointing to each attraction, clear repetition of the target phrases, and confident sounds.

“I can’t wait for the weekend! There are so many exciting things to do. I can go on a picnic, hang out with friends or play video games. What weekend activities do you like to do? I need some ideas! Let’s find out what the children will do!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.11 - B. Listen and circle

details: Listen and circle continues checking sound–image connections. Students listen for specific words or details, then show understanding by clearly circling the correct picture.
Look for accurate circling, neat pencil work, careful listening for key words, and selecting the correct pictures.
“It’s really difficult to choose what to do… What will the children decide? Can you listen closely so we can figure out what they are telling us? Then you can help me plan my weekend!”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.73 - A Cross out and write the letters

details: Cross out and write the letters reviews the spelling and meaning of weekend activity phrases by correcting the words and matching them to the right pictures.
Look for correct matching letters (a–f), clear corrections of spelling mistakes, and links between each phrase and the correct picture.
“Oh no! The weekend activity phrases are spelled wrong and mixed up. Let’s fix the words and match them to the right activities.”

Heads Up:

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.73 - B Look & write

details: Look at A and write practises writing full “I’m going to …” sentences about weekend plans using the corrected activity phrases.
Look for six complete sentences starting with “I’m going to …”, correct use of the activity phrases, capital letters, and full stops.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.12 - C. Ask and Answer

details: Ask and answer gives controlled speaking practise with the past simple by prompting students to form questions and short replies from the visuals, showing they can use the target verbs accurately in conversation.
Look for students asking the full question, answering with ‘I’m going to …,’ accurate references to the pictures, and both partners taking turns to ask and answer.
“Well I know what I’m going to do. But what about my friends? Maybe they are going to do something different… can you help me practise asking and answering to find out?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.12 - D. Ask and Answer 10m]

details: Ask and answer gives controlled speaking practise in producing accurate questions and responses with the be going to structure in the form of a board game.
Look for pairs taking turns correctly, using the target question and answer without much help, listening to each other, and speaking in clear sentences.

“I want to play a game with my friends to find out their plans - it’s the Weekend Activity board game! Each space shows a different activity. When you land on a picture, ask and answer about what you’re going to do.”

Chant provides the opportunity to use the target language and vocabulary in a chant, as well as practising listening and reading skills.
Look for students chanting together, keeping the beat, reading accurately, and using good pronunciation as they follow the lyrics.
“We’re turning our weekend plans into a song. Let’s chant together and say what we’re going to do this weekend with our friends and family.”
